quest.title: The Dark Side of Memory
quest.description: After repairing the giant cannon and successfully dispersing the Wild Hunt, you make for Hiisi Island to attempt to get some clarity regarding the memories of your spaceship.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act II
chapter.title: Elegy of Dust and Lamplight

talks.objective: Go to Hiisi Island and give the medicine to Lauma

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see now... What's changed since we were gone?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not as much as I'd imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. If anything, looks like things are settling down. That's Lauma for ya!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Lauma. We're back!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How have things been these past few days?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The clean up work has been much more complicated than I expected. Solving problems that have built up over time is a tall order, to say the least...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I believe it will take a few weeks more. Fortunately, those who remained appear to have shaken off the initial confusion and are becoming more proactive by the day.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It's as if they've finally been forced to come face-to-face with what their faith actually is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And it's all thanks to you!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: No, I... I should have done this a lot sooner.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I've been focused on taking care of myself these past few days, so I'm in a good place. And since you're looking after the Moon Marrow for us, I should be able to help you investigate the truth of the past.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for remembering.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, have you heard anything new about that phantom?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I've tried asking around, but to no avail.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: What about you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We haven't made much progress either, but here's what we've got...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I think I've got the gist of it... Sounds like you've got your work cut out for you too. Don't forget to take good care of yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #In any case, come this way, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you see?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is... Nod-Krai? This all looks familiar...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is that... a shooting star in the sky?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (No, wait! That's our spaceship!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it over already?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: This appears to have occurred a long, long time ago. The memories I sensed are highly turbulent and disordered, so that is all my power allows me to discern.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (At least we now know where our spaceship landed in Nod-Krai... Near Starsand Shoal, or so it seems.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(That matches with what {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} told me... But I want to know more...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The flowers changed color...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (These flowers are a reflection of The Damselette's powers. Does that mean she's...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I remember her mentioning that she wanted to use the Moon Marrow to restore some of her power...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we should go see her, and see if we can help her in some way.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'll leave that in your hands, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, wait — here you go! This is the medicine you asked the Curatorium of Secrets to help prepare earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Ah. Thanks for coming all this way with it. You've been a huge help.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Also... If I may, I have a feeling that "Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar" might be able to help you get a more detailed glimpse at the memories about your spaceship.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, that's true. She's the Kuutar, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we'd best check if she's doing okay first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seeya later, then!

talks.objective: Go to the Silvermoon Hall to see The Damselette

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh? What did you just say? Would you mind... repeating that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err... That's your... ex-colleague? So... we were on Starsand Shoal together, and she was beaten by the Wild Hunt too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you just... laugh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (She totally did!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you two on bad terms, or something?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: No... I simply imagined the put-out expression she must have worn in that moment, and found it... interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She seemed quite shaken.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, she'll adjust soon enough. She's very good at that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Okay, anyway... We've gotten off topic. Now that we know how dangerous the guy targeting the Moon Marrow is... You sure you wanna carry it around with you, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: If Fatui intelligence is to be believed, Rerir would prevail even if all of Nod-Krai were to stand against him.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Perhaps something restricts him... if only for the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Before I decide, there's a favor I'd like to ask you, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #Do you think you'd be able to show me what happened when my {M#sister}{F#brother} and I arrived in Nod-Krai? I mean, when our spaceship first landed?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was quick!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: As I said — this, to me, is but a single ray of moonlight. Nothing to it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Give me your hand, and ready yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is what we saw before, only clearer...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It seems we landed safely, at least...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A lot of time appears to have passed...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(We're still inside the spaceship. To think we were in there for so long... When did {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} get out, I wonder?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Wait. Is that... {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}!?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But, how can that be? No one left the ship from the moment we landed... The door hasn't even been opened yet!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where... is this?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}! Come on! We have to leave this place!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—Hey! Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Our spaceship... A long, long time passed after we landed...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #No one left the ship during that time, but {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}... found me from outside of it, somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? How would that even be possible?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't know...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The secrets within memories are like cookie crumbs. Take a bite, and they go everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's... something seriously strange going on here. I have to get to the bottom of this.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But as Nefer said, there'll be nothing to investigate if Nod-Krai is destroyed first...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright. I'll keep the Moon Marrow with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Well, if you say so, Paimon can't stop you, but still... oooh...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Will you need my help?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Help with...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I could help you conceal the Marrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You could? That'd be great!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Detecting it within you is already no easy task, but I can teach you to further conceal its presence using kuuvahki.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Like this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Looks like a shield!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This... feels so soft and gentle... just like the moonlight...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Can you sense it? Now, try to maintain it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You learn quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Looks pretty sturdy. Could probably be used in self-defense in a pinch, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for teaching me that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you always here, Columbina? It's kinda dangerous out there, sure, but have you, like, taken a walk outside or something?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Dislike strangers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And where do we rate on that scale?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Slightly better.

choices.text: Once this whole business with the Wild Hunt is over...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! The Frostmoon Scions have changed since you last saw them. Who knows, you might actually like 'em.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I will consider it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She seems kinda tired...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Probably hasn't spoken this much in a while...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Either way, thanks for agreeing to help us.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: ...It wasn't much.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The flowers here... They like guests like you.

choices.text: Let's go out for a walk...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... She doesn't look so good...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: S—Sorry for disturbing you, but are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Has your condition worsened?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Dizzy.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...It's like... I'm returning to the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, it's not that bad, is it!?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm? I... sense the moon's power... within you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We got the Moon Marrow back from the Fatui. Can it help you in any way?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mmm... And what do you require this time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, don't even think about that. Right now, you gotta focus on getting better!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Has this just become habitual for her, after living in relationships of mutual benefit for so long...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I might need your assistance in the future.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Oh. Very well.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Give me your hand.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: *exhale* ...Back to earth. My thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, your feet never left the ground... But anyway, feeling any better?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Significantly.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The moon within your body... it is as silent as a reflection in the water... Fascinating.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I merely drew forth a ray of its light from the water. Enough to keep me tethered to the ground for now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think I sensed some other changes as well...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: That is the "Moon Goddess's Favor." All things I come into contact with will bear this mark.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It is harmless, and will fade over time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, do you wanna be the Moon Marrow's custodian, now that you've got your power back?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's supposed to be something that belongs to a "god" in any case, right?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It is the remains of Aria, Goddess of the Eternal Moon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So it does have to do with... Wait, what!?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Did you not know this already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lauma just said it was different from the other fragments, and that she could sense divine power within it.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: And she is correct. When I drew that ray of moonlight from the Marrow, I also drew some memories from within.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: That is how I know that it belongs to the Goddess of the Eternal Moon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Lauma also saw the past by using the Moon Marrow. Why didn't she see that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Lauma mentioned that she could only catch brief, blurry snippets... Perhaps this is something that only a Moon Goddess could sense...)

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: There were once three moons in the sky, each belonging to a goddess who ruled over it.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But after the war of funerary flame, all three lay slain, and two of the three moons were shattered during the conflict.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: After Aria's death, her power coalesced into this Moon Marrow...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The Iridescent Moon's remains have never been found, and while the Frost Moon's goddess died herself, her moon was never broken.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: As the prophecy stated, this moon would birth a new deity sooner or later — the entity the Frostmoon Scions call the "Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar."

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I can sense that my power belongs to the Frost Moon. But it lies beyond the false sky, too distant from me.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Forget "controlling" it... "Sensing" it alone requires immense effort.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Wait, l—let Paimon count this up... We have the Eternal Moon's Marrow with us, no one can find the Iridescent Moon's... Does that mean you have the Frost Moon's Marrow inside you, then?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: No. It can only form after the moon goddess is dead. Consider it a form of energy core.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: You may as well ask if there are rocks on the moon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you're saying that you represent the Frost Moon's power, right?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Yes. Now, a god with a Gnosis is named an Archon... Since you bear the Moon Marrow, does that make you a "Moon Goddess"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I doubt that's the same thing...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: You do not wish to become one?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not really the problem here! Also, why are you so eager to pass that title on to someone else!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, never mind this "becoming a Moon Goddess" stuff for now. We're asking if we should return this Moon Marrow to you.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I do not desire it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Nor does it desire to come to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And... What does that mean?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: When I came into contact with its power, I sensed a kind of... "rejection."

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I can only guess that this is because I, too, am a Moon Goddess. Two moons will not rise at the same time, let alone consume one another.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Guess it's stuck with me for now, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You sure that's gonna be okay? Lauma did say that you've hidden its power well, but The Damselette sensed it just fine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And it's the Wild Hunt we're dealing with here, not some run-of-the-mill enemy. If it detects the Marrow...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The Wild Hunt? You speak of that phenomenon as if you were describing a person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it sure looks like there's a person behind it all — someone with a super clear goal, too. They've been after the Moon Marrow non-stop!

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: That seems to ring a bell...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Does it really?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: My colleagues used to mention someone, back when I was still with the Fatui.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: He hailed from Khaenri'ah, gaining Abyssal power during the Cataclysm... and he had a consuming fixation on the moons...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Khaenri'ah? Well, we don't know if the phantom we saw has anything to do with that, but the details kinda match... What was his name?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I only know what others called him — the "Rächer of Solnari."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: One of the Five Sinners!?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Ah... There was that title too, yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh!? Wait a second... Dain mentioned him, didn't he? D—Does that mean that our enemy is Rerir, one of the Five!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If that was the case, surely he'd be stronger than this, though...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I have heard that he disappeared not long after the Cataclysm.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But when I asked my colleagues where he went, they replied, "Do you really not know?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why would they say that...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The tale of his final fate has it that he fell into the "moon's reflection," from which there can be no return.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, hold up, pause... There's just... too much information!

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I felt the same. They seemed to think that I should be the one who would know everything about the moons.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But as I said... My "prologue" lies beyond the false skies. I do not even remember my name...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Either way, following his departure, the Wild Hunt situation worsened drastically — and it has since become a byword for Abyssal disaster.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The present phenomenon may have inherited the same title, but it far surpasses its past incarnation in both scale and lethality.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh. To think that we're up against one of the infamous Five Sinners...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's way too much for us to handle! That incident on Starsand Shoal must've been luck, then... or maybe he wasn't giving it his all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And even then... He still defeated Marionette...
